lines.trans: Chef, some young woman is calling for you over there.
Who is she and what does she need?
She said that she came from television.
I do not want to talk to anyone.
She says that the matter is very important.
I currently have absolutely no time.
She is waiting for you near the main entrance.
Let her come into my office.
She asked you to come out for one minute.
Fine, Kostya, I will come over myself now.
Thank you, chef, I will convey your words.
And pour me some strong black tea.
Of course, chef, I will do it right now.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'near' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: I'm listening right by my ear.
The car is parked near the house.

examples.text: Возле дома Аникеева ходили два подозрительных человека.
examples.trans: Near Anikeev's house two suspicious people were walking.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'time', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'entrance', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: There at the cemetery is the main entrance.
Where is the entrance to the metro?
We will open this entrance right now.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

выйти.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выходить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to get out (be released)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'main' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('the main thing') (neuter главное, used as a noun) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The main thing is, don't worry.
The most important thing is the people.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to speak', forming an aspectual pair with 'сказать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to speak, to talk') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'girl'.

examples.text: Девушки, как я, у тебя не будет!
examples.trans: You'll never have a girl like me!

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'matter', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('matter, business') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('case (in court)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to wait', forming an aspectual pair with 'подождать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to expect') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

зайти.gloss: to come in, to drop in

meanings.en: to come in, to step in
meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to come in', forming an aspectual pair with 'заходить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to drop by') (to visit briefly) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'll drop by in the evening.

examples.text: Ну, как хочешь. Лидия Алексеевна, зайдите, пожалуйста!
examples.trans: Well, as you like. Lidia Alekseyevna, come in, please!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to call', forming an aspectual pair with 'позвать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
как тебя зовут? = what's your name? меня зовут ... = my name is ...
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'to' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: From French 'cabinet' (private study or office).

examples.text: Николай Филиппович, я сейчас в кабинете у мэра.
examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, I'm in the mayor's office right now.

meanings.note: declines like какой: какая-то, какое-то, какие-то

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'of course'.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'strong', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Рука у тебя крепкая, как у деда.
examples.trans: Your grip is strong, just like your grandfather's.

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('all right') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: налей мне чаю = pour me some tea; налей мужу = pour your husband a drink

examples.trans: Nina, pour your husband a drink. We've got something to celebrate!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
Secondary conversational sense ('there isn't') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
+ genitive: ни копейки = not a penny
Secondary conversational sense ('...  = neither... nor') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Пятьсот. А у меня ни копейки.
examples.trans: Five hundred. And I haven't got a penny.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun
Secondary conversational sense ('alone') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

передать.gloss: to pass on, to hand over

meanings.en: to pass on, to hand over, to give
meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'дать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to pass on', forming an aspectual pair with 'передавать'.

examples.trans: Please pass on my regards to your mum.

examples.text: Всё, я ухожу. Ребёнок ни при чём. Передай это Алексею.
examples.trans: That's it, I'm leaving. The child isn't to blame. Give this to Alexei.

meanings.en: to come up to, to approach
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ойти'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to come up', forming an aspectual pair with 'подходить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to suit, to fit') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Нам не нужна ваша приставка! Ещё раз подойдёте к моему ребёнку — пожалеете!
examples.trans: We don't need your console! Come near my child again and you'll be sorry!

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to come', forming an aspectual pair with 'приходить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: просить прощения = to ask for forgiveness
Secondary conversational sense ('to beg') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'straight'.
Secondary conversational sense ('straight ahead') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.note: + 3rd person verb: 'пусть строят' = let them build

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to do', forming an aspectual pair with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Secondary conversational sense ('tell me / tell us') (polite request) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: 'дать слово' = to give one's word, 'держать слово' = to keep one's word
'дать слово' = to give one's word, 'держать слово' = to keep one's word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'completely'.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town.
This is a completely new car.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города. И предложение у меня к вам такое.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town. And my offer to you is this.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Secondary conversational sense ('? = what's this?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'television' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Телевидение покажет сюжет про вашу дружную семью.
examples.trans: Television will show a story about your united family.

examples.text: Ты будешь выступать на телевидении, Виктор.
examples.trans: You will perform on television, Viktor.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: partitive genitive чаю is common: чашка чаю

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.
Now I'll make some tea too.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('black').

examples.trans: Listen, look in the black cabinet.

examples.text: На нём был строгий чёрный костюм.
examples.trans: He was wearing a formal black suit.

examples.text: Как не нашла? Послушай, в чёрном шкафу посмотри. Там справа от двери!
examples.trans: What do you mean you didn't find it? Listen, look in the black cabinet. There to the right of the door!

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
